summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms include 日 with 月, associated with brightness or dawn, and the distinct form 朙, with 月 and a window-shaped 囧, associated with moonlight through a window. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

formation.text: The early 日+月 construction is semantic: the sun and moon contribute celestial imagery associated with brightness, or with dawn in one interpretation. A separate early graph, 朙, combines the moon and a window image; it was interpreted as moonlight entering through a window. 囧 is also reported as a sound element in 朙, but that analysis remains disputed because the available sound comparison does not explain the difference between the reconstructed readings. These accounts do not establish one exclusive original construction. [ref016, ref017, ref020, ref021]

components.text: In the early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun and contributes to the celestial-light scene associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn. [ref016, ref020]
In the early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon and contributes to the celestial-light scene associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn. [ref016, ref020]

In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. It is also reported as a sound element, but its proposed phonetic role is disputed: the available Old Chinese comparison differs from 明 in both initial and final, and the window's ancient spoken name is not established. [ref016, ref017, ref020, ref021]

sound_limitation.text: The reported phonetic role is not independently resolved by this evidence. The available reconstruction gives different readings for 囧 and 明, and the original spoken name of the depicted window is not established; neither fact demonstrates a historical sound correspondence. [ref016, ref017, ref021]

sound.text: The reported Old Chinese comparison is 囧 *k-mraŋʔ beside 明 *mraŋ in Baxter–Sagart 1.1; the reconstructed forms differ in initial and final, so this pair does not by itself demonstrate the reported phonetic role. [ref012, ref013, ref017]

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon and contributes to the interpretation of moonlight through a window. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

history.text: 日+月 forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Other reported early forms include 朙, with 月+囧, and less secure 目+月 and 田+月 forms. The Shuowen tradition identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙; this is one historical account, not proof that 朙 was the only early form. [ref010, ref014, ref015, ref016, ref020, ref021]

A Qin manuscript's 目-form is reported as a likely graphic corruption of 囧. This proposed change concerns the written form; it does not settle the relationship among the other early forms. [ref003, ref016, ref020]

uncertainties.text: The relative chronology of the early brightness and dawn meanings is unresolved. The proposed phonetic role of 囧 in 朙 also remains disputed, and the depicted window's original spoken name is not established. [ref016, ref017, ref020, ref021]
The early inscription readings and graphic interpretations are reported without inspection of the underlying inscriptions; exact dates for the cited examples are unresolved. [ref016, ref020]

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The evidence does not establish whether this use preceded or followed the attested dawn use. [ref016, ref020]
Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples; a cited Shijing line also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved. [ref015, ref016, ref020]
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. The evidence does not specify how this use developed from brightness or dawn. [ref016, ref020]
Modern glosses include bright, light, and clear. [ref004, ref007]

limitations.text: Both brightness and dawn are reported in early use, but their relative chronology and the development of later clear or manifest uses are unresolved. [ref016, ref020]

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms pair the sun and moon, or the moon and a window; these images are associated with brightness, dawn, or moonlight, without establishing one original meaning. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon construction. [ref016, ref020]
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon construction. [ref016, ref020]
In 朙, 囧 pictures a lattice window; its proposed sound role remains disputed. [ref016, ref017, ref021]
In 朙, 月 pictures the moon in the interpretation of moonlight through a window. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

relationships.text: In the reported early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial-light scene associated with 明. [ref016, ref020]
In the reported early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial-light scene associated with 明. [ref016, ref020]
The Shuowen account identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This reported graphic relationship does not show that 朙 was the only early form. [ref015, ref019, ref021]
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. [ref016, ref020, ref021]
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the reported moonlight-through-a-window interpretation. [ref016, ref020, ref021]
囧 is reported as a sound element in 朙, but the available same-system Old Chinese readings, 囧 *k-mraŋʔ and 明 *mraŋ, differ; the phonetic analysis remains disputed. [ref016, ref017, ref021]
